items.title: Mortgage and Loan Insurance Programs Under the National Housing Act-Debenture Interest Rates
items.summary: This notice announces changes in the interest rates to be paid on debentures issued with respect to a loan or mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration under the provisions of the National Housing Act (the Act). The interest rate for debentures issued under Section 221(g)(4) of the Act during the 6-month period beginning January 1, 2026, is 4 percent. The interest rate for debentures issued under any other provision of the Act is the rate in effect on the date that the commitment to insure the loan or mortgage was issued, or the date that the loan or mortgage was endorsed (or initially endorsed if there are two or more endorsements) for insurance, whichever rate is higher. The interest rate for debentures issued under these other provisions with respect to a loan or mortgage committed or endorsed during the 6-month period beginning January 1, 2026, is 4\3/4\ percent.

trends_raw:
- **Volume and baseline:** 170 evidence candidates surfaced on 09/03/26, none of them first seen in this run, and there is no previous run in the archive. Treat this as the baseline against which the next run's newness rate gets measured, not as a slow news day.
- **Where the weight sits:** medicare medicaid at 30 items, long term care at 19, housing at 13, workforce at 12, financial security at 10, palliative hospice at 9. Payer policy and facility oversight together account for roughly half the run.
- **Coverage posture:** 82 items carry a confirmed gap and 78 sit on beats where no monitored publisher is watched at all, against 65 monitored publishers out of 132 in the registry. The two categories should be handled differently. Confirmed gaps are competitive openings. The unmonitored 78 need a coverage check before anyone claims exclusivity, and they also point at where the monitoring list is thin.
- **Contested versus open:** financial security is the most competitive beat in the run with 4 of 10 items already matched, so Social Security and SSI stories need speed or a distinct angle. Housing at 0 of 13 covered and palliative hospice at 0 of 9 are wide open. Long-term care sits between them at 2 of 19.
- **Freshness:** the long-term care cluster refreshed the same day as the run, and medicare medicaid, workforce, palliative hospice, caregiving and depression mental health all carry items 3 days old or newer. The pipeline is catching material inside the window where it still reads as news.
- **Source mix:** government APIs and regulatory filings dominate the top of the ranking, which is why 10 of the leading items support charts built directly from source files. The tradeoff is that these items arrive without key findings attached, so the analytic work is ours to do rather than something to quote.
- **Tagging note:** the workforce cluster picked up a RAND report of 08/31/26 on space defense industrial base workforce shortfalls and STEM pipelines. It is not an aging story, and it is a useful reminder that workforce as a topic label pulls in material well outside the beat.
feature_pitch_raw:
- **The strongest run-wide story:** Medicare and Medicaid pulled 9 unrelated sources into the same window, 30 items in all, and 27 of them carry a confirmed gap against 65 monitored publishers. Nothing coordinated that convergence; federal data refreshes, regulatory notices, labor statistics and policy research landed on the same subject inside a few weeks. The through line is what older adults and the operators who serve them pay, and what the public record already shows about the results.
- **Evidence on the table:** CMS refreshed its Medical Equipment Suppliers dataset on 08/30/26, listing supplies carried by location alongside Medicare participation status, broken out to states and counties. BLS put medical care CPI at 593.78 (index 1982-84=100) for July 2026, up 1.7% year over year. The Federal Register carried the Medicare APM Incentive Payment Advisory on 08/13/26, alerting qualifying participants that CMS lacks the billing information needed to disburse payments, and the RAPID device coverage pathway notice with comment period on 08/11/26. Justice in Aging published its Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services primer for older adults on 08/20/26. KFF posted Medicaid Coverage for Women, the Medicaid/CHIP Monthly Enrollment Tracker and an analysis of rural hospitals providing inpatient maternity care in Medicaid, all on 08/26/26. The Center for Retirement Research weighed in on 08/26/26 on a proposal to shift Medicare funding to states and what that would mean for the program.
- **Why now:** the newest item in the cluster is 3 days old as of 09/03/26, and the long-term care cluster refreshed the same day the run closed.
- **Localization:** 6 of the 30 Medicare and Medicaid items break below the national level, so a single reporting pass supports state, metro or facility versions.
- **Visuals:** 10 items sit on structured public data with state and county geography, which means a ranking, map or trend line can be built from the source files rather than commissioned.
- **Also converging:** long-term care with 5 sources and 19 items, 17 with a confirmed gap; housing with 6 sources and 13 items, all 13 unmatched; workforce with 4 sources and 12 items, 10 unmatched. Palliative and hospice, at 9 items from CMS provider data and RAND, has zero monitored coverage.
pitch_ideas_raw:
- **The August 1 nursing home data dump nobody has written up.** Hook: on 08/01/26 CMS refreshed Health Deficiencies, Fire Safety Deficiencies, Penalties, Ownership, Provider Information, MDS Quality Measures, Survey Summary, Inspection Dates, Nursing Home Data Collection Intervals and Medicare Claims Quality Measures, each with three years of citations or scores and each carrying state and county geography. Angle: one accountability package that pairs citation scope and severity with fines, payment denials and current ownership, then localizes to a metro. Competitive situation: every one of these datasets is a confirmed gap, and the bundle is the single largest cache of structured, reportable material in the run.
- **Medical equipment suppliers, by county.** Hook: the highest-scoring item in the run at 74 is the CMS Medical Equipment Suppliers refresh of 08/30/26, which shows what each location carries and whether it participates in Medicare. Angle: a consumer-facing supply desert map, matched against the 65-plus counts in the ACS state profile. Competitive situation: confirmed gap, three days old, and localizable to states and counties.
- **Hospice family experience, national and state side by side.** Hook: CMS refreshed both the National and State CAHPS Hospice Survey files on 08/07/26, carrying mean scores for Medicare-certified providers. Angle: rank states against the national mean and pair the numbers with the RAND paper of 08/31/26 on how patients and family caregivers judge communication quality in tele-palliative versus in-person visits. Competitive situation: the palliative and hospice cluster has 9 items and zero monitored coverage, so there is open field on both the data and the qualitative side.
- **Pay is rising slower than the cost of care.** Hook: BLS put home health care services average hourly earnings at 27.91 dollars in June 2026, up 1.2% year over year, while assisted living and CCRC earnings reached 25.47 dollars, up 3.2%. Medical care CPI rose 1.7% in July 2026. Angle: a wage-versus-price piece that also tracks headcount, home health at 1,886.10 thousand jobs and up 4.8%, nursing care facilities at 1,592.90 thousand and up 2.6%, assisted living and CCRCs at 1,028.20 thousand and up 1.5%. Competitive situation: all four labor series are confirmed gaps, and the workforce cluster shows 10 gaps across 12 items.
- **Fair market rents set the ceiling for older renters.** Hook: HUD published FY 2027 Fair Market Rents for the Housing Choice Voucher and Moderate Rehabilitation Single Room Occupancy programs on 09/01/26, including the reevaluation procedures public housing agencies must follow under HOTMA. Angle: what the October 1 effective date means for older voucher holders, read against the disparate impact supplemental proposed rule of 08/10/26 and the FHA debenture interest rate notice of 08/21/26. Competitive situation: the housing cluster is 13 items with 13 confirmed gaps, the cleanest sweep in the run.
- **A rescinded ruling changes how rent help counts against SSI.** Hook: the Social Security Administration gave notice on 08/31/26 of the rescission of Acquiescence Ruling 90-2(2), which governed treatment of a rental subsidy as in-kind income for SSI benefit calculations. Angle: a service piece for beneficiaries and the family members helping with rent. Competitive situation: coverage is light rather than absent, so this needs a fast turn and a practical framing rather than a news lede. The related SSR 26-2p notice of 09/01/26, which rescinds and replaces SSR 11-2p on documenting disability in young adults, is a confirmed gap and can run as a companion.
- **Clinicians owed APM incentive payments CMS cannot send.** Hook: the advisory published 08/13/26 tells qualifying Alternative Payment Model participants that CMS lacks current billing information needed to disburse their incentive payments and explains how to update it. Angle: a short trade alert with the deadline mechanics, paired with the RAPID coverage pathway notice of 08/11/26 and its comment period. Competitive situation: both are confirmed gaps in a cluster where only 3 of 30 items have been matched.
- **The Medicaid access set.** Hook: four items inside seven days, the Justice in Aging HCBS primer on 08/20/26 on how home and community-based services let older adults with disabilities stay in their communities and the policy gaps limiting access, plus KFF's enrollment tracker, women's coverage data note and rural inpatient maternity analysis on 08/26/26. Angle: one explainer on where older adults sit inside a program under pressure, with the rural hospital piece supplying the geography. Competitive situation: all four are confirmed gaps.
- **The localization engine.** Hook: the ACS 2023 state aging and housing profile covers 52 states with 65-plus, 65-74, 75-84 and 85-plus counts, median household income and housing tenure, including 5,994,486 residents aged 65 and older in California and 4,630,733 in Florida. Angle: use it as the denominator under every facility, supplier and workforce story above. Competitive situation: confirmed gap, and it converts national federal data into state versions at low cost.
